title: Spices and flavours
examples: What is the difference between a spice and an herb?
Why did the spice routes become so important in history?
Can you give me an example of umami in food?

explain.say: Today we are learning about different tastes we can find in food.

draw.text: Tastes: Sweet, Sour, Salty, Bitter, Umami

explain.say: Sweet tastes are often associated with sugars and ripe fruits.
Sour tastes are often found in citrus fruits like lemons.
Salty tastes come from added salt or naturally salty foods.
Bitter tastes are sometimes found in dark chocolate or certain greens.
Umami is a savory taste often described as meaty or brothy.

faq.q: What is the difference between a spice and an herb?
faq.a: An herb is usually the fresh or dried leaf of a plant. A spice is typically the seed, root, bark, or fruit of a plant.

faq.q: Why are spices so important in world history?
faq.a: Because they were valuable and hard to get, they led to long trade routes. These routes connected many different civilizations together.
asks: What was the role of spice trade?
Why did people travel so far for spices?

faq.q: Is umami the same as salty?
faq.a: No, umami is a distinct savory taste that is different from just saltiness. It adds a deep, full flavor to food.
asks: Is umami just a strong taste?

faq.q: Do all spices come from plants?
faq.a: Yes, nearly all spices we use in cooking come from parts of plants. This includes seeds, roots, or dried berries.

faq.q: What is the best way to use spices?
faq.a: It is best to use spices in small amounts to let their natural flavour shine through. Too much can make the food taste too strong.
asks: How much spice should I use?

facts: Sweet tastes are often associated with sugars and ripe fruits.
Sour tastes are often found in citrus fruits like lemons.
Umami is a savory taste found in ingredients like mushrooms.
The spice routes were major historical trade networks.
Spices can come from seeds, roots, bark, or fruits.

quiz.say: A lemon's taste is best described as:
quiz.why: Lemons contain citric acid, which gives them a distinctly sour taste.

wrong.0: Sweetness comes from sugars, which lemons do not contain.
wrong.1: Umami is a savory taste, not the sharp, acidic taste of a lemon.
wrong.3: Salty comes from sodium, which is different from the acid in lemons.

quiz.say: Cinnamon, which comes from tree bark, is an example of a:
quiz.why: Cinnamon is the dried bark of a tree, which fits the definition of a spice.

wrong.0: While it comes from a plant, the bark itself is not classified as a fruit.
wrong.1: Leaves are a different part of the plant than the bark.
wrong.3: An herb is usually a leaf, not the bark of a tree.

quiz.say: When thinking about the historical trade of spices, what was the main reason for the routes' importance?
quiz.why: Spices were valuable and difficult to obtain, making trade along these routes very important.

wrong.0: The routes were about goods like spices, not primarily about mining for gold.
wrong.2: While new crops were traded, the primary driver was the high value of the spices themselves.
wrong.3: The silk exchange was a separate, though related, major trade commodity.
